title: Hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia (adult)
subject: respiratory
summary: Send blood and lower respiratory cultures, then start empirical anti-pseudomonal therapy chosen by MDR risk and the local antibiogram, adding a second Gram-negative agent and MRSA cover only when risk or unit resistance justifies it. De-escalate on culture results and treat for 7 days if responding.

sections.title: Recognise and assess risk
items: HAP: pneumonia developing 48 hours or more after admission and not incubating at admission. VAP: pneumonia developing more than 48 hours after starting mechanical ventilation.

Suspect when there is a new or progressive infiltrate plus at least 2 of: fever above 38 C (100.4 F), WBC above 12,000 or below 4000/microL, new purulent or changed sputum, worsening gas exchange (rising FiO2), new or worse cough or dyspnoea, crackles or bronchial breathing, unexplained confusion in the elderly (ICMR).

MDR risk for VAP: IV antibiotics in the past 90 days, septic shock at onset, ARDS before VAP, 5 or more days in hospital before onset, acute renal replacement therapy before onset. For HAP the consistent risk is IV antibiotics in the past 90 days.
High mortality risk (HAP): need for ventilatory support because of the pneumonia, or septic shock.

Common Indian ICU pathogens: Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with frequent carbapenem resistance, and MRSA. Consider mimics: atelectasis, pulmonary oedema, ARDS, pulmonary embolism, aspiration pneumonitis.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Blood cultures x 2 and a lower respiratory sample before antibiotics, without delaying treatment in unstable patients.

VAP: non-invasive endotracheal aspirate with semi-quantitative culture is preferred over invasive quantitative sampling (IDSA/ATS); bronchoscopic samples by local expertise. HAP: expectorated or induced sputum, or nasotracheal suction.
Chest X-ray (CT or lung ultrasound if unclear), CBC, creatinine, electrolytes, LFT, lactate, blood gas.
Decide to start antibiotics on clinical criteria; do not use procalcitonin to withhold treatment. Procalcitonin with clinical criteria may help stop therapy.
Know your unit antibiogram: MRSA proportion among S. aureus, and resistance of Gram-negatives to each candidate agent (the thresholds below depend on it).

sections.title: Empirical therapy (IDSA/ATS 2016)
items: Every regimen includes one anti-pseudomonal agent: piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, ceftazidime, imipenem or meropenem (levofloxacin or aztreonam in beta-lactam allergy).

Add a second anti-pseudomonal agent of a different class (amikacin, levofloxacin, ciprofloxacin, aztreonam) only for: an MDR risk factor, unit Gram-negative resistance to the first agent above 10%, or unknown local susceptibility; in HAP also for high mortality risk or IV antibiotics in 90 days. Avoid two beta-lactams.

Add MRSA cover (vancomycin or linezolid) for VAP with an MDR risk factor or unit MRSA above 10 to 20% (or unknown); for HAP with IV antibiotics in 90 days, unit MRSA above 20% (or unknown), or high mortality risk.
Low-risk HAP (no high mortality risk, no MRSA factors): single agent (piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, levofloxacin, imipenem or meropenem).
Never use an aminoglycoside as the only anti-pseudomonal agent. Consider adjunctive inhaled aminoglycoside or polymyxin for VAP due to Gram-negatives susceptible only to these.

sections.title: Indian practice (ICMR 2019)
items: Early onset or minimal prior antibiotics: cefoperazone-sulbactam or piperacillin-tazobactam, alone or with amikacin.

Late onset or prior antibiotic exposure: meropenem or imipenem-cilastatin plus amikacin; where carbapenem resistance exceeds 20%, carbapenem plus colistin or polymyxin B (consider nebulised colistin with IV colistin).

Add empirical MRSA cover (linezolid, vancomycin or teicoplanin) where MRSA prevalence exceeds 10 to 20%. Suspected VAP with septic shock and rapid deterioration: cover MRSA and carbapenem-resistant Gram-negatives with the anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam.

Culture-proven Acinetobacter, Klebsiella or Pseudomonas: one active agent by susceptibility; reserve colistin or polymyxin B for isolates resistant to all other tested drugs. CRE with septic shock: two active agents.
Levofloxacin can be an oral step-down if susceptible. Do not use faropenem as step-down for carbapenem-susceptible infection; tigecycline is not recommended routinely for VAP.

sections.title: Response, de-escalation and duration
items: Review at 48 to 72 hours: temperature, WBC, oxygenation and FiO2, secretions, haemodynamics, culture results.
De-escalate to the narrowest active agent once cultures return; stop MRSA or second Gram-negative cover when not supported by cultures.
Treat for 7 days if there is a good clinical response (IDSA/ATS; ICMR). Longer for immunodeficiency, empyema, lung abscess, cavitation or necrotising pneumonia.

Dose for renal function; in morbid obesity use dosing weight = (actual + ideal body weight) / 2 (ICMR). Monitor vancomycin levels, and renal function and neurotoxicity with aminoglycosides, colistin or polymyxin B.
Not improving: look for empyema, abscess, a resistant or unusual organism, another infection source (line, urine, sinusitis, C. difficile) or a non-infectious cause.

sections.title: Escalate
items: Septic shock or rising oxygen requirement: ICU, sepsis bundle, early source review.
Involve infectious diseases or the antimicrobial stewardship team for carbapenem-resistant organisms, polymyxin use or failure of therapy.
Pleural effusion with sepsis: ultrasound-guided aspiration to exclude empyema.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Treating a positive endotracheal aspirate without clinical or radiological pneumonia (colonisation).
Using carbapenem plus colistin reflexively in units where resistance is low, or failing to de-escalate.
Aminoglycoside monotherapy, and underdosing in obesity or augmented renal clearance.
Courses beyond 7 days in patients who have responded.

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.notes: Renal adjustment; neurotoxicity in renal failure.

drugs.name: Cefoperazone-sulbactam
drugs.notes: ICMR option for early-onset or low-exposure HAP/VAP.

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.notes: Imipenem-cilastatin 500 mg IV every 6 hours is an alternative. Renal adjustment.

drugs.name: Amikacin
drugs.notes: Second Gram-negative agent only, never alone. Monitor levels and creatinine.

drugs.name: Levofloxacin
drugs.dose: 750 mg IV or orally once daily
drugs.notes: Second anti-pseudomonal agent or step-down if susceptible; exclude TB. Renal adjustment.

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.dose: 15 mg/kg IV every 8 to 12 hours, adjusted to levels
drugs.notes: MRSA cover. IDSA/ATS 2016 trough target 15 to 20 mg/L.

drugs.name: Linezolid
drugs.dose: 600 mg IV or orally every 12 hours
drugs.notes: MRSA cover; monitor platelets. Teicoplanin 400 mg IV every 12 hours for 3 doses then 10 mg/kg once daily is an alternative (ICMR).

drugs.name: Colistin (colistimethate)
drugs.dose: 9 million units IV loading dose, then 4.5 million units IV every 12 hours
drugs.notes: Carbapenem-resistant isolates only (ICMR). Adjust maintenance for renal function; nephrotoxic and neurotoxic.

drugs.name: Polymyxin B
drugs.dose: 15,000 to 25,000 units/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses
drugs.notes: Carbapenem-resistant isolates only (ICMR). Nephrotoxic and neurotoxic; monitor creatinine.
